kurz: Why a multiple contains a valuation that others have calculated, and why your own contribution lies in choosing the comparison group.

bloecke.md:
A multiple is the result of a valuation that others have already carried out. If you value a company using its competitors' price-to-earnings ratio (P/E), you adopt their discount rate, their growth expectations and their capital structure, usually without noticing and without checking these figures. That makes multiples fast, because two figures from the annual report and a median of five comparable companies produce an assessment that takes days with a DCF. It also makes them dangerous, because you adopt other people's assumptions and mistake the result for an insight of your own.

That a multiple is a condensed valuation can be shown mathematically. For a company in a steady state, that is, with stable earnings, a stable payout and constant growth, a justified P/E follows directly from the present value model.

bloecke.formel: Justified P/E = payout ratio / (cost of equity − perpetual growth)
bloecke.erklaerung: The formula follows from the dividend discount model P = D₁ / (r − g), divided by the expected earnings of the coming year. It serves as a framework for thinking, not as a calculation rule, and applies only to mature companies with constant assumptions.
variablen: share of earnings that goes to the owners as dividends or buybacks
sustainable growth rate of earnings, g; must be lower than r
bloecke.beispiel: With a 60% payout ratio, 9% cost of equity and 2% growth, the result is 0.60 / (0.09 − 0.02) = 8.6. If g rises to 3%, it is 10.0. One percentage point more growth therefore justifies a P/E that is 17% higher.

bloecke.titel: Justified P/E at a 60% payout ratio
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation using the formula above; because the small difference r − g is in the denominator, every percentage point has a disproportionate effect.

bloecke.md:
Between the top right and the bottom left corner lies a factor of 2.25, although both corners describe an unremarkable, profitable company. A P/E difference of 10 versus 15 within an industry is therefore not yet a finding. It raises the question of whether one of the companies grows faster, is riskier or has to retain more of its earnings in the business.

The calculation can also be reversed. The trailing P/E of the S&P 500 stood at 26.07 on 18 September 2026. Assuming a payout ratio of 60%, this price corresponds to a gap between the required return and perpetual growth of 0.60 / 26.07 = 2.3 percentage points. This calculation is a plausibility check and not a valuation. To justify the price, you would have to explain why this gap stays so narrow permanently. The reciprocal of the P/E is the earnings yield, here 1 / 26.07 = 3.8%. For comparison, on 18 September 2026 ten-year US Treasuries yielded 5.01% and ten-year German federal bonds around 3.5%.

Every multiple condenses assumptions about growth, risk and capital requirements into a single number. Two companies with different P/E ratios are only more or less expensive than each other if these three drivers do not differ.

## Choosing the peer group

In a valuation with multiples there is only one substantive decision, namely which companies form the comparison group (peer group). All further steps are arithmetic. What matters for the selection is the driver profile, that is, growth, margin, capital intensity, return on capital, cyclicality, regulation and currency area. The industry label alone is not enough. Added to this is technical comparability. Financial statements under HGB (Commercial Code) and IFRS differ systematically in goodwill, development costs, leases and pensions. Time series that extend across the year 2019 also contain the break caused by IFRS 16, which increased EBITDA, total assets and net debt at the same time.

bloecke.titel: Peer group of a specialty chemicals company (illustrative calculation)

bloecke.md:
In margin, growth and leverage, the company being valued lies between Peer B and Peer C. The median of 12.5 is therefore a reasonable starting figure. The arithmetic mean of 13.3 is not suitable for this, because Peer E alone pulls it upwards. With a 16% margin and 9% growth, Peer E runs a different business.

The company being valued has revenue of €2,400 million, EBITDA of €380 million and depreciation of €140 million, giving EBIT of €240 million. After interest and 31% income tax, net profit is €141 million; with 60 million shares, that is €2.35 per share. The book value of equity is €1,100 million, which includes €400 million of goodwill. Net financial debt is €600 million, minority interests €40 million and the share price €34.00.

The peer median gives an [[enterprise value]] of 12.5 × 240 = €3,000 million. After deducting net financial debt and minority interests, €2,360 million of equity value remains, or €39.33 per share. The medians of the other multiples for the same group lead to different values.

bloecke.titel: Value per share from five multiples
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation of the implied value per share from the medians of the same five comparable companies.

serien.name: Implied value per share in euros

bloecke.md:
The range runs from €29.33 to €41.33, so the highest value is 41% higher than the lowest. All five figures are based on the same company, the same comparison group and the same reference date. The differences have explainable causes, and understanding these causes is the most important insight the method provides.

- The value from EV/EBITDA is below the one from EV/EBIT because the comparable companies are more depreciation-intensive. Their ratio of EBITDA to EBIT is 12.5 / 7.5 = 1.67, while that of the company being valued is only 380 / 240 = 1.58. An EBITDA multiple from a more capital-intensive group systematically undervalues a less capital-intensive company.
- The P/E contains the financing and the tax rates of the comparable companies, because price and earnings are both figures after interest and taxes. Where leverage differs, it is the least precise of the five multiples.
- The P/B gives the lowest value because the company being valued earns more on its book value than the comparable companies. Its return on equity is 141 / 1,100 = 12.8%, while the peer medians of P/B and P/E imply only 1.6 / 15.0 = 10.7%. The €400 million of goodwill in the book value raises the value from P/B here. A book value measures historical acquisition costs, not earning power. For businesses with high intangible assets it is therefore largely meaningless.
- EV/Sales contains an assumption about the margin. At the median margin of 11%, the peer median of 1.3 corresponds to an EV/EBIT of 11.8. That is close enough to 12.5 to confirm that the group is internally consistent.

bloecke.erklaerung: Every sales multiple implicitly contains an assumption about the margin. Only when you work out this assumption do you know what the valuation rests on.
bloecke.beispiel: EV/Sales of 1.3 at a 12% margin corresponds to an EV/EBIT of 10.8. If the margin falls permanently to 6%, the same sales multiple corresponds to an EV/EBIT of 21.7. The price is unchanged, but measured against operating profit the valuation has doubled.

bloecke.md:
The choice of comparison group has the strongest influence on the result and is at the same time the least documented step of the valuation. If the group is put together to fit the desired result, almost any value can be produced without a single number being falsified.

A few rules help against this. Selection criteria and the multiple are set down in writing before you see the result. The group comprises at least five to eight companies. The median is used instead of the mean, and the full range is reported, not just the median. Companies with a negative denominator or one close to zero are excluded instead of being included with absurd values. All figures come from one source and one reference date. Damodaran reports an aggregate P/E of 34.22 for the US market for January 2026, because he sums market value and earnings across all listed companies, including the loss-makers. At multpl.com, the P/E for the S&P 500 on 18 September 2026 is 26.07. Both figures are correct, but they cannot be compared with each other.

## Limits of relative comparison

A multiple only shows whether a company is priced higher than a group of other companies. It does not answer what the company is worth. If the whole group is too expensive, the method delivers a value that is too high, and that value looks as precise as any other result. One example is the telecom shares of 2000, which were valued consistently with one another. Every valuation with multiples therefore needs two reference points. The relative one is the peer group; the absolute one is a DCF, or at least a check of which growth and margin assumptions are embedded in the multiple.

## P/E of cyclical companies

A second source of error lies in the denominator. Cyclical companies look cheapest precisely when their earnings cannot be repeated. This is shown by an illustrative cyclical company over eight years, whose share price fluctuates less than its earnings because the market partly anticipates the cycle.

bloecke.titel: Illustrative cyclical company over eight years, P/E in two versions (average earnings €2.30)
Two price-to-earnings ratios for the same company
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation in which the P/E on annual earnings is lowest in the year of peak earnings, while the P/E on smoothed earnings is almost at its highest there.

bloecke.md:
The two series lead to opposite conclusions. In year 5, the year with the highest earnings, the unsmoothed P/E of 9.1 shows the cheapest value of the entire period, while the smoothed P/E of 18.3 shows almost the most expensive. In year 8, after the collapse in earnings, it is the other way round. Investors who buy cyclicals on the basis of the current year's P/E therefore systematically buy in the wrong phase of the cycle.

## Shiller CAPE for the overall market

If you apply this smoothing to the overall market and a period of ten years, you get the cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings ratio. It divides the inflation-adjusted price by the inflation-adjusted average earnings of the last ten years. How necessary this smoothing is can be seen from the unsmoothed trailing P/E of the S&P 500. It stood at 123.73 in May 2009 because earnings had collapsed. The shares themselves were not expensive at the time.

bloecke.titel: Shiller CAPE of the US stock market, 1900 to 2026
bloecke.unter: Annual values; the dashed line shows the historical mean of 17.42. Source: multpl.com.

bloecke.md:
On 18 September 2026 the CAPE stands at 40.94. That is 2.35 times the historical mean of 17.42 and well above the median of 16.13. The value is only 7% below the all-time high of 44.19 from December 1999. The lowest value was 4.78 in December 1920.

Less follows from the high level than the number suggests. Over a horizon of one to two years, the CAPE has historically had hardly any predictive power. The correlation only appears in real subsequent returns over ten years or more. Even this finding is less firmly established than the usual scatter plots suggest, because 126 years contain only about twelve non-overlapping ten-year windows. From this you can derive an expectation, but not a rule for action.

In the annual values since 1992, the CAPE was below its historical mean only once, in 2009. With the rule of not being invested whenever it is above the mean, you would have been out of the market for three decades.

In addition, there are comparability problems that limit how meaningful the pre-war values are. These include changed depreciation and impairment rules, a collapse in earnings in 2008/09 that remained in the ten-year window until 2018/19, share buybacks, lower corporate tax rates and an index composition that has shifted from capital-intensive industry to capital-light businesses with a high return on equity. These objections do not make the CAPE worthless, but they mean that a direct comparison with 1929 is not sound. All CAPE values given here refer exclusively to the US market. Comparable series for Germany or Europe were not available for this lesson, and the US levels cannot be transferred to the DAX.

## A multiple set by law

In Germany there is a multiple that is laid down in law and not derived from a peer group. For unlisted interests in corporations and partnerships, inheritance and gift tax is based on fair market value (gemeiner Wert). If there has been no sale between unrelated third parties within the last year, Section 11(2) BewG (Valuation Act) permits the simplified capitalised earnings method (vereinfachtes Ertragswertverfahren) under Sections 199 to 203 BewG.

bloecke.formel: Capitalised earnings value = sustainably achievable annual earnings × 13.75
bloecke.erklaerung: Annual earnings are derived from the operating results of the last three financial years (Section 201 BewG), which are first adjusted for special items (Section 202(1) BewG). A flat-rate income tax expense of 30% is deducted from this (Section 202(3) BewG). The capitalisation factor of 13.75 has been laid down in Section 203(1) BewG since 2016.
bloecke.beispiel: With adjusted annual earnings of €400,000 after the flat-rate tax deduction, the capitalised earnings value is 400,000 × 13.75 = €5.5 million.

bloecke.md: The fixed factor of 13.75 corresponds to a capitalisation rate of 7.3%. It was introduced because the factor previously derived from the base rate (Basiszins) kept rising as interest rates fell and produced obviously excessive values. Since then it has applied unchanged, regardless of the level of interest rates. Measured against an average cost of equity for mainly German companies of 9.7% (KPMG Cost of Capital Study 2025), the factor is high, which increases the value for tax purposes. The asset-based value (Substanzwert) under Section 11(2) sentence 3 BewG is only a minimum value and therefore does not cap the value. An upper limit is set by Section 199(1) BewG, under which the method may not be applied if it leads to obviously inaccurate results. An expert valuation under IDW S1 (the valuation standard of the German Institute of Public Auditors) using the capitalised earnings method or DCF is then required. In appraisal proceedings (Spruchverfahren) over compensation payments, too, the multiples method regularly serves only as a plausibility check. In German valuation practice, multiples are therefore used as a check, while the decision rests on present values.

schritte.titel: Choose a reference figure that suits the business
schritte.text: Value capital-intensive businesses using EV/EBIT or the free cash flow yield, not EV/EBITDA. Normalise strongly fluctuating earnings first.

schritte.titel: Define the peer group and write it down
schritte.text: Set the criteria of growth, margin, capital intensity, cyclicality and accounting standards before seeing the result. Select five to eight companies and use all data from one source and for one reference date.

schritte.titel: Calculate the median and check the dispersion
schritte.text: If the multiples are far apart, the group is not suitable as a peer group. In that case, look for the reason instead of calculating an average.

schritte.titel: Calculate the bridge to equity value carefully
schritte.text: From the enterprise value, deduct net financial debt, minority interests and, depending on convention, pension obligations, and add non-operating assets. Divide the result by the diluted share count.

schritte.titel: Report a range instead of a point value
schritte.text: Calculate at least two multiples and explain the difference. A valuation presented as a single number suggests a precision that the method does not have.

bloecke.md: Multiples are not suited to determining value, but they are very good at raising questions. A company trading at half the peer median is therefore not necessarily cheap. In such a case, either the market is wrong or your own comparison group is. The valuation begins with clarifying which of the two possibilities applies.

mitnehmen: A multiple condenses assumptions about growth, risk and capital requirements into a single number (justified P/E = payout ratio / (r − g)).
The choice of peer group determines the result and should therefore be set down in writing before you see the value.
For the same company and the same comparison group, five multiples give values of €29 to €41 per share; a problem only arises if this range is concealed.
Cyclical companies look cheapest when their earnings are highest; the only remedy is normalised earnings in the denominator.
The Shiller CAPE of 40.94 in September 2026, compared with a historical mean of 17.42, supports an expectation for ten years, but not a signal for the next twelve months.

begriffe.text: Valuation using comparative ratios. The median of a multiple from a peer group is applied to the corresponding figure of the company being valued. The method provides a relative classification, not an absolute value.
Group of comparable companies whose multiples are used for the valuation. What matters is similarity in growth, margin, capital intensity and risk, not the industry label.

Cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings ratio, calculated as the inflation-adjusted price divided by the inflation-adjusted average earnings of the last ten years. It smooths out earnings cycles but is not suitable for timing purchases and sales.
P/E divided by the expected earnings growth rate in percentage points. The ratio takes account of neither risk nor capital requirements and fails with low or negative growth.

Tax valuation method under Sections 199 to 203 BewG. The sustainably achievable annual earnings are multiplied by the statutory capitalisation factor of 13.75; the asset-based value serves as the minimum value.
